description: From smaller problems to smarter solutions.
outline: Tracing calls and the call stack
Memoization and a first look at dynamic programming

steps.title: A small starting point
steps.description: This practice question lets you try the learning tools. The full lesson will be added here next.
steps.question: What is the base case in this function, and why does it need one? Assume n is a non-negative integer.
hints: Look for the branch that returns without calling factorial again.
What happens when n reaches zero? Think about what would happen without that check.
steps.solution: The base case is n == 0, which returns 1. Each recursive call reduces n by one, so a non-negative integer eventually reaches zero. The base case stops the recursive calls; without it, calls would continue with negative values until Python raises a RecursionError.
